title: Brow seam closed: rock shaded from the ground, not the skyline
question: Left tile of each pane, about a third across — the vertical seam should be gone and nothing else should have moved. Does that hold, and does the rock read the same everywhere else?
context_md:
You said do it, so it is done and pushed.

`World::ground_datum`, frozen at genesis beside `sky_surface`: **the top of the lowest run of cells the sky cannot reach**, each column walked up from the bottom until an outdoors cell stops the walk. `light_datum` is built from that instead of the skyline.

A brow is skipped because open air sits under it; a cave is not, because cave air is not outdoors and the walk carries straight through; a notch is untouched, so the opening still has the same job. Stored history, no inference, no width threshold, ~8 KB and one genesis scan. **Draw cost unchanged** — 16.69/16.73 ms against 15.3–16.8 before.

| seed | rock un-darkened by >=8 rows | >=24 (visible) | largest patch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 48,114 | 2,958 | x 518..523, y 144..639 |
| 3 | 25,476 | 5,394 | x 493..502, y 97..639 |
| 5 | 39,644 | 2,987 | x 332..337, y 139..639 |
| 7 | 35,449 | 982 | x 1941 (one column), y 146..639 |

### Two things I got wrong on the way, both recorded

**The first metric was a tautology and read as a triumph.** After the fix the probe said **0 over-darkened cells on every seed** — because it compared the grade's depth against the walk-up depth, and the new datum is *defined* as the top of the walk-up run. Same arithmetic twice; zero whatever the code does. It reports the size of the *correction* now, which is non-zero for a real reason and returns to zero if the datum is ever reverted.

**The first guard sampled where the ramp is flat and passed with the bug still in.** Rock fifty rows down under a brow against fifty rows down in a plain column: depths plainly wrong (115 against 55), brightnesses 241 against 248 — under 3%, inside tolerance, green. The grade is a smoothstep flat at both ends, so a sixty-row error costs almost nothing near the floor and **~36% ten rows down**. Moved to ten rows down it reads 237 against 378 and fails hard.

That corrects how I sized this for you earlier: "worst 37 rows" was the wrong number. What matters is *where on the ramp* those rows sit — the seam is loudest just under the surface, where you actually stand, and fades to nothing at depth. So it was somewhat more visible than I told you, not less.

761 tests, clippy and docscheck clean, acceptance clean apart from the pre-existing `wood` case.
